name: Acropolis of Athens
description: The ancient citadel perched above the city, home to the Parthenon and Greece's most iconic ruins. A must-see for any first visit to Athens.

name: Parthenon
description: The 5th-century BC temple dedicated to Athena, the defining symbol of ancient Greek architecture, sitting atop the Acropolis.

name: Acropolis Museum
description: A modern glass-and-concrete museum displaying artifacts unearthed from the Acropolis, including original Parthenon sculptures.

name: Ancient Agora of Athens
description: The former civic and commercial heart of ancient Athens, where Socrates once taught, now an open-air archaeological park.

name: Plaka Neighborhood
description: Athens' oldest neighborhood, a maze of narrow lanes, neoclassical houses, tavernas, and souvenir shops beneath the Acropolis.

name: National Archaeological Museum
description: Greece's largest museum, housing an unparalleled collection of antiquities including the Mask of Agamemnon.

name: Temple of Olympian Zeus
description: The towering remaining columns of what was once the largest temple in ancient Greece, near the city center.

name: Panathenaic Stadium
description: The all-marble stadium that hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896, still used for ceremonial events.

name: Mount Lycabettus
description: The highest hill in Athens, reachable by funicular, offering panoramic sunset views over the whole city and the sea.

name: Syntagma Square
description: The central square in front of the Greek Parliament, known for the hourly changing of the Evzones presidential guard.

name: Monastiraki Flea Market
description: A lively bazaar-style market of antiques, street food stalls, and vintage shops in the shadow of the Acropolis.

name: Benaki Museum
description: A private museum tracing Greek art and history from prehistory to the 20th century, set in a neoclassical mansion.

name: Museum of Cycladic Art
description: A boutique museum devoted to the minimalist marble figurines of the Bronze Age Cycladic civilization.

name: Hadrian's Arch
description: A Roman triumphal arch marking the boundary between the old Greek city and the new Roman city built by Emperor Hadrian.

name: Kerameikos Archaeological Site
description: The ancient cemetery and potters' quarter of Athens, a quiet, less-crowded ruin site with an on-site museum.

name: Areopagus Hill
description: A rocky outcrop near the Acropolis where the ancient council once met; a free, quiet spot with sweeping city views.

name: Anafiotika
description: A tiny, whitewashed Cycladic-island-style neighborhood tucked into the slopes below the Acropolis, easy to miss but full of charm.

name: National Garden of Athens
description: A shaded, green public park behind the Parliament building, a peaceful escape from the summer heat with ponds and small ruins.

name: Varvakios Central Market
description: Athens' bustling fish, meat, and produce market, an authentic and sensory local food experience.

name: Byzantine and Christian Museum
description: A museum dedicated to Byzantine art and religious artifacts spanning over a thousand years of Greek Christian history.

name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center
description: A striking modern cultural complex by the sea with a park, canal, and the National Library and Opera House.

name: Piraeus & Mikrolimano
description: Athens' historic port district, with a picturesque marina lined with seafood tavernas, easily reached by metro.

name: Cape Sounion & Temple of Poseidon
description: A dramatic clifftop temple ruin overlooking the Aegean Sea, a popular half-day trip especially at sunset.
